batched_path.how_to_use_collect_logits: from strands_decider.data.format import Example; from strands_decider.evaluate import collect_logits, predictions_from_logits. Build Example(kind='choice', state=<text>, instructions=<question>, options=[[name, description], ...], label=<int index into options>); description may be ''. Prompt text is rendered by the package itself (Example.to_question -> prompting.render_state/render_question), so no manual formatting. Call collect_logits(model, examples, device='cuda', batch_size=N, max_length=model.config.max_length): the default max_length=3072 is NOT the model's 4096 window, so always pass it. It returns raw untempered logits (columns past each row's option count hold -1e4), labels, n_slots, examples; options are never shuffled in eval. Apply temperature with predictions_from_logits(logits, labels, n_slots, examples, temperature=model.config.temperature_by_kind): divides logits by the per-kind temperature (choice=0.8177 for v21) then masked softmax. predictions_from_logits returns Prediction objects with .probs, .pred. collect_logits uses the model on its current device but does not use the engine's prefix cache or fp32 handling (cuda keeps bf16 torso, fp32 head).

findings.batching: engine.ask(state, {name: Question}) takes ONE state and N questions; questions are batched (max_batch=32) and share the state's KV cache (use_prefix_cache). No API for several states per call: multi-state batching needs custom code or one call per state.
findings.context_note: state is truncated to fit; question keeps first claim
findings.probabilities: ChoiceAnswer.probabilities: dict option -> probability (softmax, temperature calibrated), plus .choice (argmax) and .confidence; ScoreAnswer.probabilities keyed by level index with .legend; NoulAnswer.noul = P(true).
